grants.description: Verify your identity using your National Insurance number, date of birth, and full name
grants.purpose: To confirm you are the person who received the benefit decision and can request reconsideration

grants.description: Share details of the original benefit decision you are challenging
grants.purpose: To identify which decision is being challenged and verify eligibility for mandatory reconsideration

grants.description: Consent to a full review of your benefit claim with risk of decreased or stopped benefit
grants.purpose: Mandatory reconsideration reviews your ENTIRE claim, not just one aspect. Your benefit may stop, stay the same, increase or decrease.

grants.description: Provide your explanation of why you believe the decision was wrong
grants.purpose: To give DWP decision-makers your reasons for requesting reconsideration

grants.description: Share any new or additional evidence to support your mandatory reconsideration request
grants.purpose: To provide evidence that was not included in the original decision or supports your disagreement

revocation.mechanism: Contact the DWP office handling your request by phone or letter before the mandatory reconsideration notice is issued
revocation.effect: Your mandatory reconsideration request will be cancelled and the original decision will stand. You may still have time to submit a new request if within the 1-month time limit.

delegation.limitations: Agent CANNOT proceed past the risk acknowledgment without your explicit consent that you understand your benefit may decrease or stop. Agent CANNOT accept a negative mandatory reconsideration outcome without your explicit decision on whether to appeal to tribunal. Agent CANNOT provide legal advice - you should seek free advice from Citizens Advice or a legal adviser. Agent CANNOT pay for medical evidence on your behalf.
